title: Camp 4 close: he goes before you (Mark 16)
hook: the women at the tomb hear he goes before you into Galilee

segments.voice: Yesterday, truly this man: a Roman soldier at the cross said indeed this man was the son of God. Your line was the soldier saw. Who did you look at again? Today the camp ends, at an empty tomb. Day two hundred thirty-one.

Very early on the first day of the week, just as the sun is rising, three women walk to the tomb with spices to anoint the body: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome. They had watched the crucifixion from a distance. On the way they worry about something practical: who will roll the stone away for us? It was very big. They're not expecting a miracle. They're expecting a heavy rock and a dead friend. Then they look up, and the stone is already rolled back.
screen: `SUNRISE, THE FIRST DAY OF THE WEEK.` → `WHO WILL ROLL THE STONE AWAY?` → `IT'S ALREADY ROLLED BACK.`

segments.voice: First, the news. Inside, a young man in a white robe is sitting on the right, and they're terrified. He says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Be not affrighted; you seek Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified: he is risen, he is not here." Second, the errand: "But go, tell his disciples and Peter that he goeth before you into Galilee; there you shall see him, as he told you." And Peter. The one who wept by the fire is named on purpose. Not left out. And Galilee is where it all began: the lake, the boats, the ordinary towns. He's not waiting in the Temple. He's gone ahead, back to the everyday. Third, the ending. The women run from the tomb, trembling, "and they said nothing to any man; for they were afraid." In the oldest manuscripts we have, Mark stops right there. Later manuscripts carry a longer ending, with the risen Jesus appearing first to Mary Magdalene, and sending the eleven out to the whole world. The Catholic Church receives that longer ending as inspired Scripture, and scholars still debate who wrote it and when. Either way, the good news didn't stay silent. You're hearing it. Fourth, look back. This camp was the text itself. The Psalms: two ways, the Lord ruleth me, be still, have mercy, out of the depths, let every spirit praise. Then Mark straight through: the beginning, fishers of men, the sower, peace be still, Ephphatha, who do you say I am, Bartimaeus, the widow's mites, Abba, truly this man. And now, he goes before you. Tomorrow a new camp begins, the depths, starting with how Catholics pray when words run out.
screen: `HE IS RISEN, HE IS NOT HERE.` · `TELL HIS DISCIPLES, AND PETER.` · `THEY SAID NOTHING; THEY WERE AFRAID.` · `THE PSALMS, THEN MARK STRAIGHT THROUGH.` · then, large: `HE GOETH BEFORE YOU INTO GALILEE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: go back to your ordinary Galilee. Settle and breathe. Your Galilee is the place you spend most of your days. A kitchen, a desk, a car, a classroom, a checkout line. Picture it clearly. Now imagine that someone has gone ahead of you and is already there, waiting, before you arrive tomorrow. Catholics say the risen Christ goes before them into ordinary life. If you pray, you can ask to see him there. If you don't, just picture walking into your ordinary place expecting something good. The bell holds the time.
Camp four close. The end of the text: the Psalms, then Mark straight through, ending at an empty tomb and a message: he goes before you. Today's word.
Your line: he goes before you. Tomorrow morning, when you walk into your most ordinary place, pause at the door for one breath before you go in. Day two hundred thirty-one.

howItsDone: Catholics celebrate the resurrection at the Easter Vigil and on every Sunday, and the resurrection is the first Glorious Mystery of the rosary; Mark 16 is read at the Easter Vigil in the year of Mark.

fork.setup: you're one of the three women. the stone is rolled back, a young man in white says he is risen, and to go tell the others. what do you do?
options: run and tell everyone right away.
flee, trembling, and say nothing, because you're afraid.
stay and wait inside the tomb.
fork.reveal: "and they said nothing to any man; for they were afraid." in the oldest manuscripts, Mark ends right there. clearly, someone spoke eventually.

original.note: Greek: he goes before you, as a shepherd goes ahead of the flock.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Easter story, with an ending missing.
what it means: he is risen and has gone ahead to ordinary Galilee, with words for the disciples that name Peter, the one who failed.
what a scholar hears: Sinaiticus and Vaticanus end at 16:8; 16:9–20 is held canonical in Catholic teaching, under Trent's decree on the books 'with all their parts'; proagei echoes 14:28.
